ai_regulation_level: Development of the most advanced AI should be paused until safety rules are in place.
Major new AI systems should have to pass testing and get approval before release.
AI should face targeted rules for specific harms, like fraud and discrimination, enforced by existing agencies.
There should be few or no new AI rules; the industry should develop and fix problems as they come up.
ai_state_laws: States should be free to pass AI laws stricter than federal law.
States can pass their own AI laws until there's a federal one, which would then take over.
One national AI standard should override state AI laws.
ai_china_race: Competing with China shouldn't affect US AI safety rules at all; safety comes first.
US AI rules should avoid putting US companies far behind China, but safety still matters.
Staying ahead of China in AI matters more than most safety concerns.
ai_licensing: The most powerful AI systems should need government approval, after government safety testing, before release.
The most powerful AI systems should need a license from an independent safety body, not a government agency.
No approval needed, but companies must test the most powerful systems for dangers and report the results to the government.
The most powerful AI systems should face no requirements beyond existing laws.
ai_open_release: Companies shouldn't be allowed to publish their most powerful AI models for anyone to download and change.
Companies can publish their most powerful models for anyone to download, but only after safety testing.
Companies should be free to publish any AI model for anyone to download and change, even though safety limits can then be removed.
ai_job_loss: If AI replaces many jobs, the government should mainly slow the use of AI to replace workers.
If AI replaces many jobs, the government should mainly expand income support, like cash payments to people who lose work.
If AI replaces many jobs, the government should mainly fund retraining and help workers find new jobs.
If AI replaces many jobs, the government should do little, because new jobs will appear as with past technology.
ai_layoff_limits: Employers replacing many workers with AI should owe notice and severance, and some jobs, like teaching and nursing, shouldn't be replaced by AI at all.
Employers replacing many workers with AI should owe advance notice and severance pay, but no jobs should be off-limits.
There should be no legal limits on employers replacing workers with AI.
moderation_false: Large social media companies should remove much more legal but false content than they do now.
Large social media companies remove about the right amount of legal but false content now.
Large social media companies should remove less legal but false content and leave most of it up.
Large social media companies should remove only illegal content, leaving up legal posts even when they're false.
moderation_offensive: Large social media companies should remove much more legal but offensive content, like insults aimed at a group, than they do now.
Large social media companies remove about the right amount of legal but offensive content now.
Large social media companies should remove less legal but offensive content and leave most of it up.
Large social media companies should remove only illegal content, leaving up legal posts even when they're offensive.
moderation_law: The law shouldn't limit what large platforms remove; companies decide what they host.
Large platforms should have to explain why they remove posts or ban users, and let users appeal.
The law should ban the largest platforms from removing legal political posts.
platform_liability: Social media companies should be legally responsible for harmful content their own systems recommend or promote.
Social media companies should be responsible only if they're told about clearly illegal content and don't remove it.
Social media companies shouldn't be responsible for what users post; the users are.
social_media_min_age: There should be no legal minimum age for social media; parents decide.
The legal minimum age for social media should be 13.
The legal minimum age for social media should be 16.
The legal minimum age for social media should be 18.
age_verification: Adult websites shouldn't have to check users' ages; parents should use controls at home.
Adult websites should have to check ages, using methods that don't need ID, like estimating age from a face scan.
Adult websites should have to check ages with a government ID or something similar.
algorithm_bias_testing: AI used to screen job or loan applicants should be tested for bias by independent auditors, with the results made public.
Companies should have to test their screening AI for bias themselves and keep records.
Companies shouldn't have to test screening AI for bias; existing anti-discrimination laws are enough.
data_centers: New AI data centers should be limited until there's enough clean power for them.
New data centers should be allowed, but should pay the full cost of the new power plants and lines they need.
Approvals for data centers and power plants should be sped up to keep the US ahead in AI.
election_deepfakes: Anyone who shares unlabeled AI-made fake video or audio of a candidate in the months before an election should face penalties.
Campaigns and paid advertisers should have to label AI fakes of candidates, but ordinary people who share them shouldn't be penalized.
There shouldn't be a special law; existing fraud and defamation laws are enough.
automation_tax: Companies should pay a special tax when machines take over workers' jobs, with the money supporting workers who lose jobs.
There shouldn't be a special tax, but tax breaks that favor machines over workers should end.
There shouldn't be a tax on replacing workers with machines, because it would slow productivity growth.
crypto_rules: Cryptocurrency companies should be regulated like stock exchanges and banks.
Cryptocurrency should face light rules focused on fraud.
Cryptocurrency shouldn't face any special rules.
digital_dollar: The Federal Reserve should create a digital dollar that people can hold in an account with it.
The Federal Reserve should create a digital dollar only with strict privacy protections.
A government digital dollar should be banned.
ai_copyright: AI companies should need permission from creators and pay them to train on their books, art and articles.
AI companies should pay creators for training on their work, but shouldn't need permission.
AI companies should be free to train on published work without permission or payment.
ai_companions_minors: AI friend or romantic-partner chatbots should be banned for anyone under 18.
Minors can use AI companion chatbots with parental consent and safety limits.
AI companion chatbots should be allowed for minors, with parents deciding at home.
